passage:
I’m ten, and I still remember pushing into the canteen line on Friday. The bell for maths was about to ring, so I slid in between Aadhya and a Class 8 boy and held out my coins. Nobody spoke at first. Aadhya just looked at me. Then someone behind us said, “The line starts back there.”
My face went hot. Part of me wanted to shout that I was in a hurry, and part of me felt very small. The Class 8 boy shrugged, but I picked up my coins and walked to the back. I got my samosa late. The hungry feeling was gone by afternoon, but the other feeling stayed longer.
— Sarita

qa.q: Where did Sarita push into the line, and why?
qa.a: Sarita pushed into the canteen line because the bell for maths was about to ring.

qa.q: What was Sarita feeling when the heat rose in Sarita's face?
qa.a: It was a mix of defiance and guilt. Part of Sarita wanted to shout about the hurry, and part felt very small.

qa.q: What choice changed how the moment ended for Sarita?
qa.a: Walking to the back of the line instead of arguing let Sarita put things right, even though the samosa came late.

qa.q: How might Aadhya have felt when Sarita slid in?
qa.a: Aadhya may have felt annoyed or ignored. Aadhya did not speak but just looked at Sarita, which shows Aadhya noticed and did not like it.

grounding: Shows a child cutting a line in a hurry, feeling defiance and guilt, and reacting to how the others responded.

passage:
Note, Wednesday, Class 5. After games, Gautam stepped in front of three classmates at the water cooler and said, “Just one sip, I’ll miss my bus.” Two children groaned. A quiet girl at the back lowered her bottle and stared at the floor. Gautam saw their faces and went red. His arms crossed, and he looked ready to argue.
I did not scold him in front of the others. I walked over and said, “The line starts back there. What are you hurrying for?” He said he was afraid the bus would leave. He went to the end of the line, and afterwards he told the group he was sorry.
Tomorrow I will let the bus monitor call his row first if time worries him.
— Minakshi, class teacher

qa.q: What did Gautam say when he stepped in front of his classmates?
qa.a: He said, “Just one sip, I’ll miss my bus.”

qa.q: What was Gautam probably feeling as he stood with crossed arms and a red face?
qa.a: He was likely feeling defiant and embarrassed at once. He went red after seeing the faces around him, yet he still looked ready to argue.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped Gautam go to the back of the line?
qa.a: The teacher spoke to him privately and asked what he was hurrying for instead of scolding him publicly, which let him say he was afraid of missing the bus.

qa.q: How might the quiet girl at the back have felt when Gautam stepped in?
qa.a: She may have felt unfairly overlooked but too shy to say anything. She lowered her bottle and stared at the floor instead of speaking up.

grounding: Shows a child cutting a line out of hurry, feeling defiance and guilt, and a teacher's calm response.
